chapter: Black writers, Harvard and Down Beat
title: The power of a Down Beat review: Charlie Ventura
summary: He realized the economic power of his reviews when Ventura's manager complained.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: That’s a great insight. So you took over from him. So clearly, to the musicians, it was like a new regime in town. Again, I think it was important . . .

That’s my next question, but I just wanted to comment, parenthetically for the people listening to the interview, that they really must understand the tremendous importance of Down Beat to that world at that time.

Oh yeah. I used to – I had to review it, because it came in, but I never understood Charlie Ventura. I thought it was mainly playing notes at a hard tempo, and loud. One day his manager called me up and said, “What have you got personally against Charlie? You’re really hurting him economically.” I said, “I never met the guy.” In that sense I realized I had power. That’s what led to my brooding about it after a while.
